title: ALMA Discovery of Dust Belts around Proxima Centauri
question: Does Proxima Centauri host circumstellar dust belts (a Kuiper belt analog), and what are their location, temperature and mass?

what.value: Stellar parameters (Teff, mass, radius, luminosity) and SED photospheric model giving 74±4 uJy at 1.3 mm

evidence.quote: giving an extrapolated flux density at 1.3 mm of $74\pm4\,\mu$Jy

what.value: Proper motion and parallax for phase-center tracking

evidence.quote: proper motions of $-$3775.75 and 765.54 mas yr$^{-1}$ (van Leeuwen et al. 2007)

what.value: Solar Kuiper belt mass ~1e-2 Earth masses for comparison

evidence.quote: This mass is similar to that of the solar Kuiper belt ($\sim10^{-2}~M_\ensuremath{\oplus}$; Bernstein et al. 2004)

recipe.goal: Image and measure source flux and position
recipe.method: Multifrequency synthesis CLEAN images; IMSTAT for flux densities, IMFIT for positions and sizes
Compare ALMA 12-m peak and photospheric model prediction with ACA flux
Optically thin dust mass formula with T_d(r) law; total mass scaled via collisional cascade up to 50 km
assumptions: kappa_nu = 2 cm^2 g^-1; size distribution power-law index -3.5

recipe.goal: Search for outer belt in ACA data
recipe.method: Azimuthal averaging over elliptical annuli with a grid of PA and eccentricity
key_parameters: best PA ~140 deg, i ~45 deg, peak at ~23''
assumptions: Circular belt tilted; T_d ~10 K with same temperature law

evidence.quote: The source has a flux density of $340\pm60$ $\mu$Jy.
A secondary source with a flux density of $38\pm10$ $\mu$Jy is marginally detected
we obtain $T_d\simeq40$ K and a dust mass $m_d\simeq4\times10^{-6}~M_\ensuremath{\oplus}$.
we obtain a total mass of $m_{\rm tot}\simeq10^{-2}~M_\ensuremath{\oplus}$.

evidence.loc: 3.3 A Possible Outer Belt at 30 au
evidence.quote: we estimate a total flux density of $\sim$ 1.7 mJy

evidence.loc: 3.3 A Possible Outer Belt at 30 au
evidence.quote: corresponding to a total mass (including large bodies) of $0.33~M_\ensuremath{\oplus}$
